# math/big

> Big integers: whole numbers of any size, for when 64 bits aren't enough.

truck [math](../math.md) · [source](../../../registry/math/big.pkg)

```
let f = big_new(1)
for i = 2 to 30
  f = big_mul(f, big_new(i))
end
print big_str(f)                        // 265252859812191058636308480000000
let ok = false
let x = big_parse("-123456789012345678901234567890", &ok)
print big_str(big_div(x, big_new(1000)))  // -123456789012345678901234567
print big_str(big_pow(big_new(2), 100))   // 1267650600228229401496703205376
```

A `ptr Big` never changes: every operation makes a new one.

| function | gives |
|---|---|
| `big_new(n: int) -> ptr Big` | `n` as a big integer |
| `big_parse(s: str, ok: ptr bool) -> ptr Big` | read decimal digits with an optional sign (`_` allowed between digits); `*ok` false if it isn't a number |
| `big_str(a) -> str` | decimal digits, `-` first if negative |
| `big_add(a, b)`, `big_sub(a, b)`, `big_mul(a, b)` | sum, difference, product |
| `big_div(a, b)`, `big_mod(a, b)` | quotient truncated toward zero, and the remainder with the sign of `a`, like `/` and `%`; dividing by zero stops the program with `panic: big integer division by zero` and status 2 |
| `big_pow(a, e: int)` | `a` to the power `e >= 0` |
| `big_cmp(a, b) -> int` | negative, zero or positive |
| `big_eq(a, b) -> bool`, `big_is_zero(a) -> bool`, `big_sign(a) -> int` | comparisons |
| `big_neg(a)`, `big_abs(a)` | `-a`, `\|a\|` |
| `big_to_int(a, ok: ptr bool) -> int` | back to an `int`; `*ok` false if it doesn't fit |

Numbers are stored in base 10^9 limbs. Multiplication is schoolbook, and
division long division, so they slow down with thousands of digits.

## Library code

Merged into every program that uses this package.

```
const BIG_BASE = 1000000000

struct Big
  neg: bool
  d: [int]
  n: int
end

// big_make: a magnitude with room for n limbs, all zero
fn big_make(n: int) -> ptr Big
  let b = new Big
  let k = n
  if k < 1
    k = 1
  end
  b.d = make([int], k)
  b.n = n
  return b
end

// big_trim drops leading zero limbs; zero is never negative
fn big_trim(b: ptr Big) -> ptr Big
  while b.n > 0 && b.d[b.n - 1] == 0
    b.n = b.n - 1
  end
  if b.n == 0
    b.neg = false
  end
  return b
end

fn big_new(n: int) -> ptr Big
  let b = big_make(3)
  b.n = 0
  b.neg = n < 0
  // work with the negative value, so the most negative int fits
  let x = n
  if x > 0
    x = 0 - x
  end
  while x != 0
    b.d[b.n] = 0 - (x % BIG_BASE)
    x = x / BIG_BASE
    b.n = b.n + 1
  end
  return big_trim(b)
end

fn big_parse(s: str, ok: ptr bool) -> ptr Big
  *ok = false
  let i = 0
  let neg = false
  if len(s) > 0 && (s[0] == '-' || s[0] == '+')
    neg = s[0] == '-'
    i = 1
  end
  let digits = sb_new()
  let last_ = '_'
  while i < len(s)
    let c = s[i]
    if c == '_'
      if last_ == '_'
        return big_new(0)
      end
    elif c >= '0' && c <= '9'
      sb_byte(digits, c)
    else
      return big_new(0)
    end
    last_ = c
    i = i + 1
  end
  let ds = sb_str(digits)
  if len(ds) == 0 || last_ == '_'
    return big_new(0)
  end
  let b = big_make((len(ds) + 8) / 9)
  // limbs from the right, nine digits each
  let end_ = len(ds)
  let k = 0
  while end_ > 0
    let start = end_ - 9
    if start < 0
      start = 0
    end
    let v = 0
    for j = start to end_ - 1
      v = v * 10 + (ds[j] as int - 48)
    end
    b.d[k] = v
    k = k + 1
    end_ = start
  end
  b.neg = neg
  *ok = true
  return big_trim(b)
end

fn big_str(a: ptr Big) -> str
  if a.n == 0
    return "0"
  end
  let b = sb_new()
  if a.neg
    sb_byte(b, '-')
  end
  sb_int(b, a.d[a.n - 1])
  let i = a.n - 2
  while i >= 0
    let part = str_from_int(a.d[i])
    for k = len(part) to 8
      sb_byte(b, '0')
    end
    sb_add(b, part)
    i = i - 1
  end
  return sb_str(b)
end

// big_mcmp compares magnitudes
fn big_mcmp(a: ptr Big, b: ptr Big) -> int
  if a.n != b.n
    return a.n - b.n
  end
  let i = a.n - 1
  while i >= 0
    if a.d[i] != b.d[i]
      return a.d[i] - b.d[i]
    end
    i = i - 1
  end
  return 0
end

fn big_madd(a: ptr Big, b: ptr Big) -> ptr Big
  let n = a.n
  if b.n > n
    n = b.n
  end
  let r = big_make(n + 1)
  let carry = 0
  for i = 0 to n - 1
    let s = carry
    if i < a.n
      s = s + a.d[i]
    end
    if i < b.n
      s = s + b.d[i]
    end
    r.d[i] = s % BIG_BASE
    carry = s / BIG_BASE
  end
  r.d[n] = carry
  return big_trim(r)
end

// big_msub: |a| - |b|, for |a| >= |b|
fn big_msub(a: ptr Big, b: ptr Big) -> ptr Big
  let r = big_make(a.n)
  let borrow = 0
  for i = 0 to a.n - 1
    let s = a.d[i] - borrow
    if i < b.n
      s = s - b.d[i]
    end
    if s < 0
      s = s + BIG_BASE
      borrow = 1
    else
      borrow = 0
    end
    r.d[i] = s
  end
  return big_trim(r)
end

fn big_signed(m: ptr Big, neg: bool) -> ptr Big
  m.neg = neg
  return big_trim(m)
end

fn big_add(a: ptr Big, b: ptr Big) -> ptr Big
  if a.neg == b.neg
    return big_signed(big_madd(a, b), a.neg)
  end
  if big_mcmp(a, b) >= 0
    return big_signed(big_msub(a, b), a.neg)
  end
  return big_signed(big_msub(b, a), b.neg)
end

fn big_neg(a: ptr Big) -> ptr Big
  let r = big_make(a.n)
  for i = 0 to a.n - 1
    r.d[i] = a.d[i]
  end
  return big_signed(r, !a.neg)
end

fn big_abs(a: ptr Big) -> ptr Big
  if a.neg
    return big_neg(a)
  end
  return a
end

fn big_sub(a: ptr Big, b: ptr Big) -> ptr Big
  return big_add(a, big_neg(b))
end

fn big_mul(a: ptr Big, b: ptr Big) -> ptr Big
  if a.n == 0 || b.n == 0
    return big_new(0)
  end
  let r = big_make(a.n + b.n)
  for i = 0 to a.n - 1
    let carry = 0
    let x = a.d[i]
    for j = 0 to b.n - 1
      let t = r.d[i + j] + x * b.d[j] + carry
      r.d[i + j] = t % BIG_BASE
      carry = t / BIG_BASE
    end
    let k = i + b.n
    while carry != 0
      let t = r.d[k] + carry
      r.d[k] = t % BIG_BASE
      carry = t / BIG_BASE
      k = k + 1
    end
  end
  return big_signed(r, a.neg != b.neg)
end

// big_mul_small: |a| * m for 0 <= m < BIG_BASE
fn big_mul_small(a: ptr Big, m: int) -> ptr Big
  let r = big_make(a.n + 1)
  let carry = 0
  for i = 0 to a.n - 1
    let t = a.d[i] * m + carry
    r.d[i] = t % BIG_BASE
    carry = t / BIG_BASE
  end
  r.d[a.n] = carry
  return big_trim(r)
end

// big_mdivmod divides magnitudes: the quotient, and the remainder in
// *rem. Long division, one limb at a time; each quotient limb is found
// by binary search.
fn big_mdivmod(a: ptr Big, b: ptr Big, rem: ptr ptr Big) -> ptr Big
  if b.n == 0
    rt_panic("panic: big integer division by zero")
  end
  let q = big_make(a.n)
  let r = big_new(0)
  let i = a.n - 1
  while i >= 0
    // r = r * BASE + a.d[i]
    let t = big_make(r.n + 1)
    t.d[0] = a.d[i]
    for k = 0 to r.n - 1
      t.d[k + 1] = r.d[k]
    end
    r = big_trim(t)
    let lo = 0
    let hi = BIG_BASE - 1
    while lo < hi
      let mid = (lo + hi + 1) / 2
      if big_mcmp(big_mul_small(b, mid), r) <= 0
        lo = mid
      else
        hi = mid - 1
      end
    end
    q.d[i] = lo
    if lo > 0
      r = big_msub(r, big_mul_small(b, lo))
    end
    i = i - 1
  end
  *rem = r
  return big_trim(q)
end

fn big_div(a: ptr Big, b: ptr Big) -> ptr Big
  let r: ptr Big = null
  let q = big_mdivmod(a, b, &r)
  return big_signed(q, a.neg != b.neg)
end

fn big_mod(a: ptr Big, b: ptr Big) -> ptr Big
  let r: ptr Big = null
  big_mdivmod(a, b, &r)
  return big_signed(r, a.neg)
end

fn big_pow(a: ptr Big, e: int) -> ptr Big
  let r = big_new(1)
  let x = a
  let k = e
  while k > 0
    if k & 1 == 1
      r = big_mul(r, x)
    end
    k = k >> 1
    if k > 0
      x = big_mul(x, x)
    end
  end
  return r
end

fn big_cmp(a: ptr Big, b: ptr Big) -> int
  if a.neg != b.neg
    if a.neg
      return -1
    end
    return 1
  end
  let c = big_mcmp(a, b)
  if a.neg
    return 0 - c
  end
  return c
end

fn big_eq(a: ptr Big, b: ptr Big) -> bool
  return big_cmp(a, b) == 0
end

fn big_is_zero(a: ptr Big) -> bool
  return a.n == 0
end

fn big_sign(a: ptr Big) -> int
  if a.n == 0
    return 0
  elif a.neg
    return -1
  end
  return 1
end

fn big_to_int(a: ptr Big, ok: ptr bool) -> int
  *ok = false
  if a.n > 3
    return 0
  end
  // accumulate negatively, so the most negative int fits
  let x = 0
  let i = a.n - 1
  while i >= 0
    if x < (-9223372036854775807 - 1 + a.d[i]) / BIG_BASE
      return 0
    end
    x = x * BIG_BASE - a.d[i]
    i = i - 1
  end
  if !a.neg
    if x == -9223372036854775807 - 1
      return 0
    end
    x = 0 - x
  end
  *ok = true
  return x
end
```
